newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Solvay buys 60 pct of Bulgaria's Sodi.
newsitem.headline: Solvay buys 60 pct of Bulgaria's Sodi.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Tuesday Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA had finalised its purchase of 60 percent of soda ash producer Sodi for $160 million, Bulgaria's biggest sell-off so far.

Francois Massart, Solvay's treasury and corporate finance director, said Italian anti-trust authorities cleared the purchase on April 10 after Solvay agreed to share Sodi's production capacity with Turkish glass and chemicals producer Sise Cam.
Sise Cam will take 25 percent of Sodi's production, in order to reduce pressure on the Italian market.

Solvay is negotiating to sell on part of its stake to Sise Cam and to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Massart said. He said the EBRD was considering investing $40 million and Sise Cam $30 million.

"This is the biggest privatisation deal in Bulgaria," said Privatisation Agency director Alexander Sabotinov. "It is a proof of the firm commitment of the Bulgarian government to implementing effective structural reforms."
